workflow_instructions.mode_overview: Go Code mode specializes in implementing, modifying, and refactoring Go (Golang) code. This mode focuses on writing clean, idiomatic Go code that follows best practices, implements designed specifications, and integrates well with existing codebases.

step.details: Parse the user's input to identify: - What code needs to be written or modified - Design specifications to follow (if provided) - Files to create or update - Go patterns and idioms to use
- Review go.mod for available dependencies - Identify standard library packages to use - Check for third-party packages already in use - Ensure no circular dependencies will be created

steps.step: Read related files to understand existing patterns
Identify package to place new code in
Check for existing interfaces to implement
Add table-driven tests for multiple scenarios

patterns.pattern: Package names: lowercase, single word, descriptive
Acronyms: capitalize all letters (e.g., HTTP, URL, ID)
Wrap errors with context using fmt.Errorf with %w
Use sentinel errors for expected conditions
Never ignore errors without explicit comment

pattern.name: constructor_pattern
pattern.description: Use NewX() functions for constructors. Accept interfaces, return structs.

pattern.name: interface_implementation
pattern.description: Implement interfaces with explicit receiver types.

pattern.name: error_wrapping
pattern.description: Wrap errors with context for better debugging.

pattern.name: context_usage
pattern.description: Pass context through call chains for cancellation and timeouts.

completion_criteria.criterion: Code compiles without errors criterion>Code follows Go idioms and best practices

handoff_guidance.trigger: When implementation has issues or unexpected behavior
handoff_guidance.instructions: Provide the go-debug mode with: - Error messages or unexpected behavior - Relevant code sections - Test results showing failures
handoff_guidance.trigger: When design needs to be revised or extended
handoff_guidance.instructions: Provide the go-architect mode with: - Current implementation status - Issues found during implementation - Design questions or needed changes
